public_payload.normalized_proposition: Outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, Microsoft, Google and Amazon do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues, and the only way to get that revenue is to feed money to one or both of those companies.

statement.excerpt: That was a lot of numbers, so let me make it simpler: outside of OpenAI and Anthropic, these three companies do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues, and the only way to get that revenue is to feed money to one or both of these companies.

from_speaker: do not appear to be significantly increasing their revenues
the only way to get that revenue
feed money to one or both of these companies
our_interpretation: The three companies are Microsoft, Alphabet/Google, and Amazon.
Read the statement in its cloud and AI context, rather than as a claim that unrelated retail or advertising revenue is stagnant.
Assess realized cloud revenue growth excluding both named customers. Examine backlog separately because the preceding argument uses remaining performance obligations; backlog is not realized revenue.

Use January–March 2026, the latest reported quarter before publication. The surrounding argument emphasizes sequential backlog changes; comparable prior-quarter revenue is therefore the principal growth comparison, with year-over-year figures supplementary.
Significant means commercially substantial growth, without imposing an invented numerical cutoff.
The funding clause asserts necessity. Investments alongside commercial agreements alone do not prove that necessity.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable customer-level records show little cloud revenue growth outside both labs, and financing records establish that the relevant lab spending depended on funding from these cloud providers.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable records establish substantial cloud revenue growth outside both labs, or establish that the relevant revenue was obtained without the asserted necessary funding.
